title: KV cache namespace hash collision causes cache-miss storm during private runtime upgrade
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: During rollout of runtime-2.4.1 to private/VPC clusters we introduced a change to the KV cache key normalization (compact hashing) intended to reduce memory usage. The new normalization unintentionally collapsed tenant-scoped cache namespaces for certain prefix shapes, producing persistent hash collisions. The result was a massive cache-miss storm which amplified backend GPU worker load, exhausted request queues, and caused control plane RPC latencies to spike. Customers on private clusters experienced elevated 502/504 errors and prolonged request latencies for ~42 minutes before automated rollback and throttling mitigations restored stability.
incident_timeline: 2026-03-10T02:12Z: Runtime-2.4.1 rollout started to private clusters via canary wave 1
2026-03-10T02:24Z: Alert: control-plane request latency > 3x baseline for private cluster 'us-east-2-vpc-12'
2026-03-10T02:26Z: PagerDuty triggered; initial triage identified spike in model inference GPU utilization and a surge of requests to the model workers
2026-03-10T02:33Z: SRE attached flamegraphs and noticed KV cache miss rate increased ~1200x compared to baseline
2026-03-10T02:40Z: Mitigation: halted rollout and rolled back runtime change in affected canary clusters
2026-03-10T02:45Z: Automated rate-limiter and admission throttles triggered to shed excess load
2026-03-10T02:54Z: Control plane latencies returned toward baseline; customer-facing errors reduced but follow-up investigation continued
2026-03-10T03:30Z: Post-incident RCA session started; root cause hypothesized as cache key normalization collision across tenant namespaces
root_cause: A code change to KV cache key normalization used a compacted hash that dropped tenant namespace separators for certain prefix patterns (eg. tenantID:prefix->hashed key). This introduced deterministic collisions across different tenants when prefixes shared byte patterns that collided under the new hash. The cache subsystem lacked a per-tenant namespace enforcement and the unit test coverage did not include cross-tenant collision scenarios for the new hashing behavior.
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Reverted runtime-2.4.1 change because risk of cross-tenant collisions and customer impact was unacceptable
Short-term: add conservative enforcement of explicit tenant namespace prefixing in cache keys and reintroduce previous hashing until comprehensive tests and sharding are in place
Long-term: implement per-tenant sharding with separate cache namespaces and a strictly stable hashing function; accept the slight memory increase in exchange for correctness
Trade-off: more memory per shard vs. risk reduction for collision-induced miss storms and the operational cost of rollback during production upgrades

ENG-451011: Implement tenant-aware cache namespace prefixing enforcement in runtime (owner: Priya Nair) - estimate 5
ENG-451012: Roll out per-tenant cache sharding prototype and benchmark memory/latency tradeoffs (owner: Platform Performance) - estimate 8
ENG-451013: Add automatic circuit-breaker to throttle inference requests when KV cache miss rate crosses threshold (owner: SRE) - estimate 5

ENG-451015: Add dashboard and alerting for cross-tenant identical cache keys and sustained miss-rate deltas (owner: Observability) - estimate 3
ENG-451016: Postmortem review with customer success for affected customers and follow-up SLA credits where appropriate (owner: Customer Success) - estimate 1
followup_notes: We discovered the unsafe assumption: compact hash reduced key entropy but also removed an explicit tenant separator in a internal optimization path. That path was not exercised by existing regression suites because tests ran single-tenant workloads.
Engineers added blocked-by gating to the runtime upgrade pipeline to require canary telemetry for KV miss-rate, GPU queue depth, and control plane RTT before promoting to subsequent waves.

A temporary mitigation is in place: the runtime will enforce an explicit tenant prefix on all cache keys (configurable flag) and the compact-hash path is disabled by default until sharding is implemented.
We validated the rollback by replaying sample workloads against a staging private cluster and observing stable miss rates and bounded GPU utilization.
Root cause blames: code regression in hashing logic + insufficient cross-tenant test coverage + upgrade pipeline not gating KV-specific metrics
review_feedback: PM (Riley Chen): prioritize per-tenant sharding and observability as P1 for next cycle
SRE (Lara Kim): require improved release gating for runtime changes that touch cache key space
Security (Omar Aziz): confirm no sensitive tenant data could have been exposed due to key collisions (audit complete; no data leak found)
Design (Evelyn Park): request clearer telemetry naming conventions for tenant-scoped metrics
